followups.area: feed admission snapshot, journal commit boundary, and provider-health projection

sourceToPipeline.localFinding: Feed committed an observation to canonical ingress, immediately marked its signature seen, then wrote Census-R. If that secondary write failed, the method returned canonical ACCEPTED without exposing incomplete projection and same-process retry was suppressed. In the live path, provider health was also refreshed before Census-R, so a failed secondary projection could still mint a fresh validated-observation timestamp.
sourceToPipeline.existingOverlap: Canonical ingress remains the durable acceptance authority. Census-R remains a secondary ordered projection. The change exposes post-commit incompleteness and lets an identical canonical duplicate retry that projection; it does not turn secondary-journal success into LIVE feed evidence.
risks: The Census-R journal used in this path is not proven crash-durable by this test; process restart may require separate recovery design.
A canonical ACCEPTED receipt can now carry a warning because downstream local projection is incomplete; callers must inspect postCommitWarning.
Historical retries must not update live freshness, provider health or slot watermark.
A live provider observation must not refresh provider capability health until canonical ingress and Census-R projection both commit.
Queued feed work must own snapshots of caller-provided log arrays and raw payload bytes, while checking queue capacity before allocating copies.
validationRequirements: Inject Census-R failure after canonical acceptance and assert an explicit postCommitWarning.
Retry the same observation and require canonical DUPLICATE plus successful idempotent Census-R projection.
Assert historical failure and retry do not alter live timestamp, slot or provider health.
Inject a LIVE Census-R failure and assert Yellowstone/WSS provider health is not refreshed before both journal commits.

implementation.change: Feed snapshots source metadata, log arrays, and raw payload bytes after admission capacity succeeds and before queueing, preventing mutation while waiting under backpressure. It adds signatures to its bounded dedupe set only after Census-R succeeds; a failed side projection returns CENSUS_JOURNAL_WRITE_FAILED and remains retryable. Canonical DUPLICATE receipts proceed through the idempotent secondary projection path. Yellowstone and WSS validated-observation health updates occur only after canonical ingress and Census-R commit.

followups.area: observed wallet delta and cost conservation

sourceToPipeline.localFinding: The standalone transport settlement helper accepted one ambiguous solDeltaLamports field, subtracted fees and rent from it, and called the result an observed economic settlement. That shape could double-subtract costs if solDelta was the finalized wallet post-minus-pre delta, and it counted recoverable rent funding as friction.
sourceToPipeline.existingOverlap: This remains a standalone reconciliation helper with no production call sites. It now takes explicit gross trade SOL flow and finalized wallet SOL delta, proves exact conservation against wallet-paid fees and rent, records rent separately, and returns the already-net wallet delta without subtracting it twice.
integrationRisks: The caller must supply gross trade flow and wallet-paid cost components derived from the same finalized signature and wallet; mismatched payers or omitted movements fail conservation.
This helper is not wired into production settlement, accounting, or learning, and the check does not establish live execution readiness.
Rent is separately reported as funded capital, not trading friction; rent recovery on account closure requires a separate finalized event.
validationRequirements: Require exact equality between gross trade flow less wallet-paid base/priority/tip costs and rent funding, and finalized observed wallet delta.
Reject a delta that subtracts fee or rent components twice.
Keep token-denominated Token-2022 withheld fees out of SOL totals and bind every settlement field into its hash.

implementation.change: Replaced the ambiguous input contract with GrossTradeSettlementEvidence. Settlement now checks conservation, reports observed wallet delta as net proceeds without a second deduction, excludes rent deposits from trading friction, and hashes explicit gross flow, observed delta, fee attribution, and rent funding.

followups.area: bounded feed ingress, historical/live health isolation, and restart-safe recovery

sourceToPipeline.localFinding: The feed accepts observations through canonical ingress and projects them into Census-R. Process-local queue overflow or a durable journal/projection failure must be visible as an ingress incident; historical repair must not advance live timestamps/provider health. A restart must not infer a clean session solely from a healthy newly constructed Feed.
sourceToPipeline.existingOverlap: Canonical ingress remains the durable observation authority, Census-R remains an ordered secondary projection, and the staging batch capability remains replay-only. The new session latch is a restart-safety marker, not evidence that a historical observation is live or that live trading is ready.
discoveries: Feed admission is bounded by item count and bytes, snapshots mutable source data only after capacity is available, and shares an in-flight result for duplicate signatures.
Provider health updates only after accepted LIVE canonical ingress and Census-R projection; HISTORICAL_REPAIR does not update live freshness or provider health.
A feed-session sidecar is written atomically and fsynced before subscription startup; unresolved ACTIVE/INCIDENT state restores an explicit hold on restart.

Yellowstone SubscribeRequest.fromSlot is used as an inclusive restart/reconnect cursor only after canonical ACCEPTED/DUPLICATE receipts; replay through the sampled confirmed boundary is marked HISTORICAL_REPAIR, and a coarse sidecar checkpoint survives clean restart. This cursor does not establish contiguous coverage.
patterns: Keep replay intent explicit and separate live-health state from historical coverage.
Use bounded serial admission with backpressure, immutable queue snapshots, and drain-on-stop.
Persist recovery uncertainty independently of the main queue so storage pressure cannot erase the hold; gate entries until an operator-reviewed recovery clears it.
Resume from a durable accepted slot inclusively; use canonical idempotency to absorb same-slot duplicates and keep coverage certificates distinct from transport replay checkpoints.
risks: This changes canonical ingestion and Engine entry gating, so independent Astra Architecture, Verification, Risk, and Certification review is required before merge or release.
A clean simulated restart test does not prove external provider recovery, current endpoint health, or production availability.
The Windows sidecar identity and atomic-replace behavior require verification on the intended filesystem and operator recovery procedure.
validationRequirements: Build the pinned TypeScript engine and run deterministic feed, Yellowstone, canonical-ingress, Census-R, replay, and staging-batch regressions.
Exercise older/newer HISTORICAL_REPAIR and failed LIVE projection with before/after live fields, provider health, and dashboard snapshot.
Verify unclean restart blocks entries, clean drained shutdown removes only its own latch, and entry execution remains fail-closed under PAPER_MAX_RISK.
Complete independent critical-change review and release-gate evaluation before merge or deployment.

implementation.change: Added bounded feed admission/backpressure and retryable Census-R projection behavior; separated historical/live health transitions; persisted feed-session incidents across restart; added Engine startup checks for ambiguous pending canonical ingress before feed startup; and added an atomic, bounded staging batch path for deterministic replay. Added Yellowstone fromSlot replay on reconnect/restart with a confirmed-slot historical/live handoff and restart-persistent cursor checkpoint.
